A tall, soft focaccia with a crisp base. It needs very little kneading, only time.

== Ingredients ==
* 500 g strong white bread flour
* 400 ml lukewarm water
* 7 g instant yeast (one sachet)
* 10 g fine salt
* 60 ml olive oil, plus extra for the top
* 2 sprigs rosemary and a few sprigs thyme, leaves picked
* Flaky salt for the top

== Method ==
# Mix the flour, yeast and water in a large bowl. Add the salt and mix with a wet hand until no dry flour is left. The dough will be very sticky.
# Cover and rest for 30 minutes. With a wet hand, stretch one side of the dough up and fold it over the middle. Turn the bowl and repeat 4 times. Do this three more times, 30 minutes apart.
# Pour 3 tablespoons of the oil into a 23 × 33 cm metal tin. Tip the dough in, turn it to coat and leave it to rise until puffy and nearly doubled, 1 to 2 hours.
# Heat the oven to 220 °C (425 °F).
# Oil your fingers and press deep dimples all over the dough. Scatter the herbs and flaky salt, then drizzle with the rest of the oil.
# Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until deep golden. Leave it in the tin for 5 minutes, then cool on a rack.

== Tips ==
* For an overnight version, use 2 g yeast and leave the dough in the fridge after step 2 for 12 to 24 hours.
* Bakers with a [[Sourdough starter]] can replace the yeast with 100 g active starter. Expect a much longer rise.
